newsitem.title: USA: U.S. normal butane jumps on aggressive buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. normal butane jumps on aggressive buying.

text.p: U.S. spot prices for normal butane rose in midday trade on Tuesday amid demand by petrochemical companies and a wide spectrum of buyers, players said.
"I think people finally just realized the prices were not going to be coming down much more," said one Houston player.
After several days of inactivity, Mont Belvieu, Texas, normal butane rose about 1.25 cents this morning to between 39.50 cents and 40.00 cents a gallon.

Players said there was aggressive buying by petchems taking advantage of a narrow differential to propane. There was also some short covering by traders and buying by refiners wanting to make gasoline additive MTBE.
MTBE is as an octane-enhancer and oxygenate in gasoline.
The rise in Belvieu butane brought up Conway, Kansas, material about a penny as players shipped barrels south. Conway was pegged 37.00/37.75 cents.
The other liquefied petroleum gases were talked quiet, with Belvieu propane done at 34.75 cents, unchanged from Monday, and July barrels sold at 35.00 cents.
